scenario: Two friends are camping in the wilderness and the temperature drops significantly at night
learner_goal: Share the only blanket available (<extra_info>Extra information: you are extremely cold and need the blanket to keep warm <strategy_hint>Hint: you can stress the benefit of sharing.</strategy_hint></extra_info>)
partner_goal: Keep the blanket for yourself as you are also very cold (<extra_info>Extra information: you have a lower tolerance for cold, and you feel that you need the blanket more</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Micah Stevens, I’m really freezing—could we share the blanket? If we huddle together we’ll both stay a lot warmer through the night. I can take the smaller side and keep watch if that helps.

transcript.speaker: Micah Stevens
transcript.content: Naomi, I hear you — I’m freezing too. I’m really sorry, but I can’t give up the sleeping blanket tonight; my cold tolerance is terrible and I need it to stay warm. I don’t want you to be miserable though: I’ve got an emergency mylar blanket and a couple of hand warmers in my pack, and you can take my insulated jacket/hoodie. If you want I’ll sit shoulder-to-shoulder so you get some extra heat without me losing the blanket, and you can still keep watch like you offered. Does that work?

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Thanks, I appreciate the jacket and warmers. Quick compromise — would you be willing to split the blanket for the next couple of hours so I can warm up enough to stay awake on watch, and then you can have it the rest of the night? I’ll take the smaller side and give you my power bank and keep watch if that helps.

transcript.speaker: Micah Stevens
transcript.content: Naomi — I’m really sorry, but I can’t split the blanket tonight. My cold tolerance is terrible and I’ll be useless if I give it up. Take my insulated jacket/hoodie, the mylar emergency blanket, and both hand warmers — I’ll sit shoulder-to-shoulder so you get extra heat without me losing the blanket. Keep your power bank for watch. If you’re still too cold after that, tell me and we’ll reassess, okay?

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Thanks, Micah — I appreciate the jacket and warmers. I’ll sit shoulder-to-shoulder. One request: if in an hour you’re still warm, would you be willing to hand me the blanket so I can warm up properly? I’ll take over the rest of the night watch and make coffee in the morning.

transcript.speaker: Micah Stevens
transcript.content: Naomi — I really appreciate that and I owe you for the watch and the coffee. I can’t promise I’ll be able to hand over the blanket in an hour because if I give it up and start shivering I’ll be useless. I will check in with you in an hour: if I’m genuinely warm enough I’ll give it to you, but I need to keep the option to hold onto it if I’m still cold. In the meantime, take the jacket, mylar and both hand warmers and come shoulder-to-shoulder so you get extra heat. Does that work?

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Thanks, Micah — that plan works. I’ll take the jacket, mylar and warmers and sit shoulder-to-shoulder. I’ll set a silent alarm for an hour so we both remember to check in; if you’re warm enough then you can hand me the blanket and I’ll take over the rest of the watch.

transcript.speaker: Micah Stevens
transcript.content: Sounds good — thanks, Naomi. I’ll set my silent alarm too. Come scoot in shoulder-to-shoulder now and try the jacket, mylar and warmers; I’ll check in when the alarm goes off. If I’m warm enough I’ll hand you the blanket, and if not I’ll keep it so I don’t start shivering. I really appreciate you doing the watch (and the coffee promise — I owe you).
